timeline.query: priority inheritance devb-eide disk driver priority starved by higher priority CPU-bound thread, loading executable blocks

timeline.why: The program's own bug is already fixed. lowsrv used a _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY channel, and the earlier edit removed that flag so lowsrv now inherits hicli's priority. What still hangs is outside the program. The graph shows procnto (pid 1, prio 50) REPLY-blocked on the disk driver devb-eide (pid 65544). devb-eide's worker threads are READY at prio 21, and the CPU hog d0e04d (pid 204822) spins at prio 22, which run.sh sets. The disk driver never runs, so nothing more is read from /var: hicli (/var/qd/E04/hicli) is never loaded. That is why d0e04a has 0 TICKs; d0e04b and d0e04c are simply starved below 22. Message-driven priority inheritance cannot help here: no program thread sends to devb-eide, and the procnto→devb-eide send is not under program control. The only real fix is to put the hog below the disk driver's priority 21, which needs a change to run.sh. The rules forbid that, and also forbid changing the hog's priority or load in hog.c. Delaying or throttling the hog would only hide the wait. No allowed .c/.h edit removes this starvation.
